rules.accepted_credit_types: Category 1 CME relevant to current or intended specialty from ACCME-accredited and reciprocating organizations, AOA, state medical societies, AMA, ABMS/AOA/RCPSC specialty boards, Joint Accreditation; includes courses, presentations/publications, enduring materials, journal CME, skill development, performance improvement, interprofessional CE, cultural competency or implicit bias training
rules.alternatives: Initial ABMS/AOA/RCPSC board certification satisfies the whole CME requirement for that 3-year cycle; attesting to participation in recertification/MOC does the same. Controlled substance CME is still required for prescribers (unless covered within the certification process). Exempt: residency training licensees, deployed military, members of the General Assembly health committees.
rules.audit_note: Report compliance or exemption on the annual renewal form; keep records 6 years for Board inspection.

topics.who: Physicians who prescribe controlled substances: prescribing practices incl. chronic pain management (part of the 60 hours); MATE Act training counts for the cycle in which it was completed

rules.notes: One board licenses MDs and DOs. License renewed (registered) annually; the 3-year CME cycle starts on the physician's birthday following license issuance.
rules.rule_quote: A physician licensed to practice medicine in the State of North Carolina, except those physicians holding a residency training license, shall complete at least 60 hours of Category 1 CME relevant to the physician's current or intended specialty or area of practice every 3 years.
